canonicalReview.reconciliationSummary: I confirmed reviewer 2's positive claims that SQLite is the active production backing and that `npm run verify-all` currently passes, but reviewer 1's two major defects still remain supported by the current code and tests. The stale closed-chunk lower-band path is still reachable because transcript invalidation does not downgrade lower-band readiness and downstream readiness/compact consumers still accept those artifacts. The first managed capture path is still split across thread creation/session linkage and later canonical append, and a verifier reproduction against the current code left a discoverable managed thread with zero messages after the first append failed. Reviewer 2 did not provide code or test evidence that disproves either path, so the canonical result stays at revise. The migration path-option drift remains supported as a non-blocking observation.
crossStoryFindings: SQLite is the active backing across runtime capture, maintenance, smart compact, inspection, snapshot/export, and the real PI execution path, and `npm run verify-all` passed on the current codebase.

One cross-story correctness gap still remains: when a source turn projection goes stale, the chunk transcript is downgraded but detailed/brief lower-band artifacts remain selectable as ready by maintenance/readiness and compact consumers.

The first managed capture path still does not satisfy TC-3.1c's transactional cutover contract because thread creation/session resolution happens before the first canonical append succeeds, leaving an empty managed thread behind on first-append failure.
architectureFindings: The source-of-truth boundary is mostly aligned with the tech design: `thread.sqlite` is authoritative managed state and generated JSONL remains projection output; active legacy JSON writes are quarantined to migration, fixtures, exports, and generated rollout artifacts.

Closed-chunk lower-band readiness is architecturally inconsistent with transcript invalidation because `getReadyChunkLowerBandArtifact()` only checks `chunk.lowerBand[band].status/text` and ignores whether `conversationTranscript` is already non-ready.

The published migration/store path contract still drifts from implementation: `sourceThreadDir` is declared but unused, `targetDbPath` is only honored during import seeding, and operational store reads still resolve only `threads/<threadId>/thread.sqlite`.
epicCoverageAssessment: `npm run verify-all` passed during this review: 570 service tests and 15 e2e tests passed, including migration, runtime capture, maintenance, compact, inspection, snapshot/export, and real PI execution coverage.

The current suite still codifies one incorrect behavior instead of rejecting it: `tests/thread/sqlite-maintenance-row-level.test.ts:361-400` expects a chunk transcript to become `pending` while both lower-band artifacts remain `ready`.

I did not find a test that proves TC-3.1c rollback behavior for a failed first managed capture; current runtime-capture coverage proves SQLite capture, retry, and reopen behavior, but not auto-create rollback of an empty thread/session linkage after first-append failure.
productionPathFindings: No fake SQLite adapter or shadow JSON source path is hiding the production route; the PI extension defaults to `SqliteThreadStore`, and the passing gate exercised real SQLite files.
Legacy JSON source files are not being mutated on the active runtime path; remaining JSON outputs are migration, fixture, legacy-export, or generated-rollout artifacts.
A material production-path defect remains: stale lower-band artifacts can still flow into strict readiness and compact decisions after their upstream transcript has already been marked non-ready.

blockingFindings.title: Stale chunk lower-band artifacts remain selectable after upstream transcript invalidation
blockingFindings.evidence: `refreshClosedChunkFromSourceTurns()` downgrades only `conversationTranscript` when source-turn projection state is no longer ready and does not clear or downgrade `chunk.lowerBand` (`src/thread/async-thread/services/chunk-service.ts:464-488`). `getReadyChunkLowerBandArtifact()` still returns any lower-band artifact whose status is `ready` and has text (`src/thread/async-thread/domain/chunk-state.ts:83-97`), and strict readiness/compact consumers still rely on that helper (`src/thread/async-thread/services/async-thread-run-service.ts:947-1004`, `src/thread-view/services/thread-view-builder.ts:317-344`). The currently passing regression test locks this behavior in by asserting `conversationTranscript.status === "pending"` while both lower-band artifacts remain `ready` (`tests/thread/sqlite-maintenance-row-level.test.ts:361-400`).

blockingFindings.title: First managed capture is not created transactionally with its first canonical message
blockingFindings.evidence: On first live capture, the PI extension auto-creates the managed thread before capture append runs (`src/context-steward/pi/pi-extension.ts:1716-1729`). `openOrCreateManagedThread()` persists thread creation and then records the thread-id map as separate steps before returning a mutable thread (`src/thread/services/thread-service.ts:177-207`), and `captureFinalizedActivityInCurrentThreadOperation()` declares the actor and appends the first canonical message later in a separate call (`src/thread/services/capture-service.ts:210-250`). `findManagedThread()` can reopen that created thread directly from SQLite target matching even without relying on `threadId-map.json` (`src/thread/store/sqlite-thread-store.ts:1239-1281`). Direct verifier reproduction against the current code with a forced first append failure returned `{ firstAttemptOk: false, messageCount: 0, turnCount: 0 }` while the managed thread remained discoverable, so TC-3.1c's transactional first-capture contract is still unmet.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Migration path options are published but only the default SQLite layout is operationally supported
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: The migration input type still publishes `sourceThreadDir` and `targetDbPath` (`src/thread/migration/sqlite-thread-migration-service.ts:29-34`), but `buildMigrationSnapshot()` always reads legacy state via `new FileThreadStore(input.rootDir).openThread(input.threadId)` and ignores `sourceThreadDir` (`src/thread/migration/sqlite-thread-migration-service.ts:304-316`). Import seeding honors `targetDbPath` (`src/thread/migration/sqlite-thread-migration-service.ts:511-542`), but operational SQLite store reads still resolve only `threads/<threadId>/thread.sqlite` via `resolveThreadSqlitePath()` (`src/thread/store/sqlite-thread-store.ts:632-646`, `src/thread/store/sqlite-thread-store.ts:996-1026`).

unresolvedItems: `packages/lh-context/src/core/inspectors.ts:139` still hard-codes `livePostCompactTailDetection.supported = false`, so appended live-tail detection remains unimplemented.

crossStoryFindings: SQLite is the real active backing across runtime capture, maintenance, smart compact, inspection, snapshot/export, and the long-thread E2E path; `npm run verify-all` passed.

The maintenance -> readiness -> compact chain still has one cross-story correctness gap: once a source turn projection goes stale, chunk transcript state is invalidated but downstream detailed/brief chunk artifacts can still remain eligible and be consumed as if they were current.

First-capture creation is still split across separate thread creation, thread-id mapping, and canonical append steps, so the first managed capture path does not satisfy the epic’s transactional cutover contract.
architectureFindings: The source-of-truth boundary is mostly aligned with the tech design: active managed state lives in `thread.sqlite`, while legacy JSON writes are quarantined to migration, fixtures, and explicit debug export paths.

Row-level SQLite maintenance exists, but the readiness contract is inconsistent with provenance invalidation because lower-band selection helpers only inspect `chunk.lowerBand[band].status/text` and ignore whether the upstream conversation transcript has already been invalidated.

The migration surface exposes `sourceThreadDir` and `targetDbPath`, but the implementation only fully supports the default `threads/<threadId>/thread.sqlite` topology; that is architecture drift against the published migration/store contract.
epicCoverageAssessment: Coverage is broad: the SQLite migration, runtime capture, maintenance, compact, inspection, snapshot/export, and legacy-retirement suites all ran green under `npm run verify-all`.

The suite currently codifies one incorrect behavior instead of rejecting it: `tests/thread/sqlite-maintenance-row-level.test.ts` expects stale chunk lower-band artifacts to stay `ready` after transcript invalidation.
There is no gate test proving that a failed first live capture rolls back thread creation/session linkage instead of leaving an empty managed thread behind.
productionPathFindings: I did not find a fake SQLite adapter or shim hiding the production path; runtime, compact, and `lhx` all execute against real SQLite files.
Legacy JSON source files are not being mutated on the active runtime path; the remaining JSON outputs are explicit migration/debug/export artifacts.
A material production-path defect remains: stale lower-band artifacts can still flow into strict/prepare compact decisions after their upstream transcript has already been marked non-ready.

blockingFindings.title: Stale chunk lower-band artifacts remain selectable after upstream transcript invalidation
blockingFindings.evidence: When a source turn projection becomes stale, `updateChunkState()` invalidates the chunk transcript but does not clear or downgrade canonical `chunk.lowerBand` artifacts (`src/thread/async-thread/services/chunk-service.ts:456-470`). `getReadyChunkLowerBandArtifact()` still treats any lower-band artifact with `status === "ready"` and text as eligible (`src/thread/async-thread/domain/chunk-state.ts:83-97`), and both strict readiness and compact accounting consume that helper (`src/thread/async-thread/services/async-thread-run-service.ts:947-1002`, `src/thread-view/services/thread-view-builder.ts:310-332`). The current regression test locks this in by asserting the transcript becomes `pending` while both lower-band artifacts remain `ready` (`tests/thread/sqlite-maintenance-row-level.test.ts:361-399`).

blockingFindings.title: First managed capture is not created transactionally with its first canonical message
blockingFindings.evidence: On a fresh session, the PI extension auto-creates the managed thread before any canonical append runs (`src/context-steward/pi/pi-extension.ts:1693-1729`). `openOrCreateManagedThread()` persists `createThread()` and then `recordThreadIdMap()` as separate steps (`src/thread/services/thread-service.ts:177-200`), and only afterward does capture declare the actor and append the first message in a separate call (`src/thread/services/capture-service.ts:210-250`). If that first append fails, the code returns `CAPTURE_APPEND_FAILED` but leaves the newly created thread/session linkage behind, which does not meet TC-3.1c’s transactional first-capture requirement.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Migration path options are published but only the default SQLite layout is operationally supported
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: `buildMigrationSnapshot()` always reads legacy data from `new FileThreadStore(input.rootDir).openThread(input.threadId)` and ignores `sourceThreadDir` (`src/thread/migration/sqlite-thread-migration-service.ts:304-316`). When `targetDbPath` is supplied, the importer seeds the DB there (`src/thread/migration/sqlite-thread-migration-service.ts:511-542`), but operational store reads still resolve only `threads/<threadId>/thread.sqlite` via `resolveThreadSqlitePath()` (`src/thread/store/sqlite-thread-store.ts:632-646`, `996-1026`).

unresolvedItems: `packages/lh-context/src/core/inspectors.ts:139` still reports `livePostCompactTailDetection.supported = false`, so appended-live-tail detection remains explicitly unimplemented.

crossStoryFindings: Epic 6 is implemented coherently across migration, runtime capture, async maintenance, smart compact, inspection, snapshot/export, and legacy compatibility surfaces. The shared runtime factory now defaults PI production capture to SqliteThreadStore, while legacy FileThreadStore usage remains quarantined to fixtures, migration input, tests, and explicit debug/export flows.
architectureFindings: The implementation preserves the tech-design invariant that thread.sqlite is authoritative managed state and generated PI JSONL is disposable projection output. Store APIs support compatibility callers plus narrower row-level turn/chunk maintenance writes, and smart compact reads through readCompactSnapshot rather than legacy JSON files or previous rollout content.

SQLite schema and store mapping cover thread identity, actors, messages, turns, chunks, imports, projection metadata, status/readiness metadata, token metadata embedded in entity records, and generated rollout linkage. Packages/lh-context has a SQLite-aware read path with dual-source warnings and optional-driver failure handling.
epicCoverageAssessment: AC-1 through AC-7 are materially covered by implementation and tests: full migration/entity preservation, runtime capture and attach/import cutover, row-level maintenance and repair behavior, strict/prepare smart compact and rollout regeneration, lhx inspection, snapshot/export, and active legacy source-truth guard coverage are all present.

Requested gate npm run verify-all passed: root verify completed with 570 service tests passing, then e2e completed with all reported suites/tests passing, including real PI execution and smart compact long-thread scenarios.
productionPathFindings: No material fake adapter, shim, placeholder, or non-real execution path was found in the active production path. Provider fakes and mocked counters are confined to tests. Legacy placeholder lower-band artifacts remain modeled for migration/inspection compatibility but are explicitly blocked from readiness and PI-target output rather than used as semantic production output.

Production PI extension defaultCreateStore returns SqliteThreadStore, active runtime/maintenance/compact guard tests prohibit hard-coded legacy JSON source paths in the active surfaces, and generated rollout JSONL remains a projection file as required.
